subject: MedScout - model fit, quantization options & pilot scope
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Hughes <sara.hughes@medscout.com>; Tom Lee <tom.lee@medscout.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: MedScout - model fit, quantization options & pilot scope

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for the demo today — good convo and helpful context on the production constraints (single-region, HIPAA-adjacent, avg doc size ~2k tokens, peak concurrent users ~300). Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Recap (call):
- Primary objective: improve triage summaries and entity extraction latency to support 300 concurrent users while keeping draft quality within current thresholds (BLEU/Rouge-ish metrics we discussed).
- Constraints: 16GB GPU memory per worker in your preferred private infra; strict PII controls; need auditability on regressions.

Recommended model path (shortlist):
1) Redwood-Open-7B (AWQ 4-bit recommended) — best cost/latency for short-form summarization with modest quality delta vs FP16 on our prompt sets.
2) Redwood-Opt-13B (GPTQ 4-bit) — for higher-quality extraction tasks where throughput can be tuned; slightly higher latency but better recall.
3) Redwood-XL-30B (FP8 or mixed FP16/FP8) — heavy-weight option for phase 2 if you need top-tier quality and can accept higher cost.

Quantization / throughput notes (summary):
- AWQ (4-bit): biggest wins for memory-constrained hosts. Typical quality drop is small on instruction-summary prompts but can be higher for edge-case entity extraction (we call these prompt family B).
- GPTQ (4-bit): slightly higher ops cost but more consistent across prompt families; better for 13B+ models.
- FP8: best fidelity for large models, useful if you can't tolerate any regression; costs more and hardware support varies.

Attachments / links I shared: prompt set (medscout_promptset_v1.txt), short eval summary (medscout_eval_summary.pdf) and the public benchmark folder (link below). Those include the prompt families we used to simulate your workload.

Proposed pilot scope & next steps:
1) Technical deep dive (90m) with Marissa & infra team — goal: validate memory/latency numbers on your infra (can we do next Tue?).
2) Pilot configuration: run 2-week hosted evaluation + 1-week private deployment canary. Metrics: token-level latency, 95th pct latency, per-prompt family quality (we'll baseline against your current system).
3) Canary safety: automatic regression alerting + holdback A/B (10% traffic holdback) during the private pilot.

Action items for MedScout:
- Confirm target week for the technical deep dive.
- Share any additional prompt families or document types we should include.

If that plan looks good I can send a short SOW and timeline.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

2) For the 16GB constraint, which of the two options (Open-7B AWQ vs Opt-13B GPTQ) gives us the best latency headroom at 95th pct?
3) What's the risk of a quality regression slipping through the baseline evals into prod? Do you recommend human-in-the-loop checks during the canary?

Sara — quick data to help with your questions (pulled from the eval we ran on the medscout prompt families attached):

Summary metrics (baseline = FP16):
- Redwood-Open-7B (AWQ 4-bit): median latency (single-token step): 9ms; p95 latency (per-request, avg doc 2k tokens): ~420ms; relative quality delta (extraction F1): -1.8% on prompt family A, -4.6% on prompt family B. Memory footprint reduced ~45% vs FP16.
- Redwood-Opt-13B (GPTQ 4-bit): median latency: 14ms; p95 latency: ~610ms; quality delta: -0.9% on A, -2.1% on B. Memory reduction ~40% vs FP16.
- Redwood-XL-30B (FP8): median latency: 32ms; p95 latency: ~1.1s; quality delta: ~0% on A/B, but cost ~3x vs 13B.

Interpreting the numbers:
- For strict 16GB workers the 7B AWQ gives the best headroom and lowest cost; the tradeoff is a non-trivial hit on the more complex extraction prompts (family B).
- The 13B GPTQ provides a safer quality profile with moderate latency overhead; it sits between 7B AWQ and 30B FP8 on quality.

On regression risk & mitigation:
- Small regressions (<2%) on family A are common with AWQ but often not user-visible; family B regressions are where human review helped catch false negatives.
- Recommended canary safeguards: 10% traffic holdback, per-prompt-family quality checks (automated), and a manual review queue for flagged degradations >2% on a rolling sample. We can wire that into your existing QA tooling and provide scripts to compute per-prompt-family metrics during the canary.

Attached: medscout_benchmarks_may2027.csv (per-prompt metrics) and a short explainer in the eval PDF.

If you'd like, for the deep dive I can run a short on-prem smoke test with a trimmed prompt subset so we can see live latency numbers on your infra (will need access to a test VM in your VPC).

—Marissa
Principal ML Engineer | Redwood Inference

1) Tech deep dive (90m) — Tue, 11 May 2027 at 15:00 ET. Owners: Marissa (ML lead), Karthik (infra lead), Tom (MedScout infra). Agenda: smoke test plan, dataset & prompt verification, canary safety checks.
2) Pilot SOW: I'll share a one-page SOW and a rough cost estimate by EOD today. High-level: 2-week hosted eval + 1-week private canary, billable evaluation credits included.
3) Pilot config recommendation: start with Redwood-Open-7B AWQ for initial throughput validation; if family B quality drops >2% we fallback to Opt-13B GPTQ for that route. We'll implement the 10% holdback and regression alerts Marissa proposed.

Please reply to confirm the Tue time or suggest an alternate slot. Also, Tom — if you can provision a test VM (16GB GPU) with SSH access for Marissa that will let us do the smoke test in the deep dive, that would speed things up.

Thanks — I'll upload the SOW + pricing + DocuSign link once Sara confirms.
